initial_plan.answerability: yes: the file has annual counts reported for motorist and cyclist deaths, allowing a direct comparison of the two groups
initial_plan.metric: annual number of reported deaths, separately for motorists and cyclists, obtained by summing number_of_motorist_killed and number_of_cyclist_killed across crash records
initial_plan.population: all crash records with a crash_date in calendar years 2013 through 2025 inclusive

data_check.facts: check_1.csv reports 2,132,218 in-scope crash rows. Neither summed death column has missing values in the population or any year; crash_date has no missing rows and no 1970-01-01 values within the population. The observed minimum and maximum dates span January 1 through December 31 in every year from 2013 to 2025.
data_check.implications_and_decisions: No in-scope rows need to be excluded or counted differently for missing or default values. Keep all in-scope crash records. The year-boundary check finds no partial year by observed date bounds, though row counts remain counts in this police-reported file.

final_plan.answerability: yes: directly compare the annual absolute number of reported deaths for motorists and cyclists
final_plan.metric: sum of number_of_motorist_killed and number_of_cyclist_killed by calendar year and category, reported as absolute death counts
final_plan.population: all police-reported crash records with crash_date in calendar years 2013–2025 inclusive; the measures count reported people killed, not fatal crashes
grouping: category derived from the motorist or cyclist killed-count field
final_plan.limitations: The file contains police-reported crashes and provides no travel-exposure denominator, so absolute counts do not compare per-trip or per-person risk; full-year date bounds do not independently establish reporting completeness. The check found no missing death-field values, no missing or 1970-01-01 crash dates within scope, and no partial years by observed date bounds, so all in-scope rows are retained.
